title: Calculate Document Edit Distance
real_world_story: An educational platform wants to measure how much one document differs from another by determining the minimum number of character changes required to transform one document into the other.

real_world_connection.system: Document comparison and text similarity system
real_world_connection.input_represents: Two document strings that need to be compared
real_world_connection.target_represents: The minimum number of edits needed to transform one document into the other
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Computing the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and replacements required between two documents

problem_statement: Given two document strings, calculate the minimum number of operations required to transform the first document into the second. The allowed operations are insertion, deletion, and replacement of a character, and each operation has a cost of 1.
task: Determine the minimum number of character-level edits required to transform the first document into the second.
input_format: The first line contains the first document string. The second line contains the second document string.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the minimum edit distance between the two documents.
constraints: Documents contain only lowercase English letters

examples.explanation: Three operations are required to transform 'kitten' into 'sitting'.
Two character replacements are sufficient to transform 'book' into 'back'.

expected_algorithm.name: Edit Distance using Dynamic Programming
expected_algorithm.reason: Each character comparison can be solved by considering insertion, deletion, or replacement, while previously computed results avoid repeated work.

hint: Create a table for prefixes of both documents.
When the current characters match, no new operation is required.
When they differ, consider insertion, deletion, and replacement and choose the minimum.
real_world_takeaway: Edit distance can help document systems measure textual differences and identify how much content has changed between two versions.
